title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten named MIT spaces for studying, collaborating, gathering, and making campus life work between classes.

cards.title: Building 14 Courtyard
cards.subtitle: Hayden Library outdoor seating
cards.notes: Use the outdoor seating for a reading break or a low-key meetup; the enclosed porch is a community space from spring through fall.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor Hayden Library setting with seasonal community space.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Libraries identifies the renovated Building 14 courtyard as having outdoor seating and an enclosed porch used as a community space in spring through fall.
cards.access_notes: Located at Hayden Library, 14S-100; review current library access policies before visiting.

cards.title: The Nexus
cards.subtitle: Hayden Library, 14S-130
cards.notes: Look for a community event or teaching session, or use the room as study space when it is not programmed for an event.
cards.short_summary: A Hayden room that shifts between events, teaching, and study.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Libraries says The Nexus is used for community events and teaching and can also be a study space.
cards.access_notes: Map-listed at 14S-130 within Hayden Library; event use may affect availability.

cards.title: Collaborative Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Hayden Library first floor
cards.notes: Bring a partner or project group: use flexible seating, whiteboards, and nearby library help for conversation-oriented work.
cards.short_summary: A 24/7 collaborative first-floor reading room in Hayden.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Libraries describes Hayden’s first-floor Collaborative Reading Room as a 24/7 space for current faculty, students, and staff with flexible seating and whiteboards.
cards.access_notes: 24/7 access is for current MIT faculty, students, and staff; follow current library access policies.

cards.title: Hayden Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Hayden Library floors 1 and 1M
cards.notes: Reserve a room when your group needs a monitor and writable planning surface; eight small-group rooms are available on floors 1 and 1M.
cards.short_summary: Reservable small-group rooms with monitors in Hayden.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Libraries states that Hayden has eight group study rooms on floors 1 and 1M, with glass walls and large wall-mounted monitors.
cards.access_notes: Reservation is required; use MIT Libraries’ study-space reservation information for current availability.

cards.title: The Loft
cards.subtitle: Overlooking Hayden’s reading room
cards.notes: Set up a class meeting or study group in the collaborative area overlooking the reading room and café seating below.
cards.short_summary: An elevated collaborative area in renovated Hayden.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Libraries says The Loft overlooks the reading room and café seating area and provides collaborative space for classes or study groups.
cards.access_notes: Located in Hayden Library; observe current library access and noise expectations.

cards.title: Quiet Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Hayden Library second floor
cards.notes: Choose this quiet zone when you need independent reading or focused work, with views toward the Charles River and Boston skyline.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet reading zone on Hayden’s second floor.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Libraries identifies Hayden’s second-floor reading room as a quiet zone with views of the Boston skyline and Charles River.
cards.access_notes: Located in Hayden Library; keep conversation and calls elsewhere.

cards.title: East Study Room
cards.subtitle: Hayden Library, MIT ID access
cards.notes: Use the windows, varied seating, and docking stations for focused laptop work; bring an MIT ID for access to this room.
cards.short_summary: An MIT-ID study room with six monitor docking stations.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Libraries describes the East Study Room as MIT-ID-access-only, with varied seating, windows, and six docking stations with 27-inch monitors.
cards.access_notes: MIT ID access only; confirm current building access before heading over.

cards.title: Barker’s Fifth-Floor Study Space
cards.subtitle: Barker Library, 10-500
cards.notes: Use the fifth-floor space for late independent or small-group work; the library says it remains available to anyone with an MIT ID.
cards.short_summary: A current MIT-ID 24/7 study option under the Great Dome.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT Libraries states that Barker Library’s fifth-floor 24/7 space remains available to anyone with an MIT ID.
cards.access_notes: MIT ID required; Barker’s stacks and service desk are closed as of March 30, 2026.

cards.title: Athena Lounge
cards.subtitle: Stratton Student Center, W20-575
cards.notes: Use this Student Center lounge as an individual or group study stop, then check the building’s current access rules before staying late.
cards.short_summary: A named Student Center lounge for individual and group study.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT’s Division of Student Life lists Athena Lounge (W20-575) among the Stratton Student Center’s individual and group study spaces.
cards.source_title: Student Center | MIT Division of Student Life
cards.access_notes: Located in W20-575; building access can require card access outside general hours.

cards.title: Stratton Reading Rooms
cards.subtitle: Stratton Student Center, W20-540
cards.notes: Meet a classmate or settle into a study session in the Reading Rooms, then use the Student Center directory to find W20-540.
cards.short_summary: Named study rooms in MIT’s central student hub.
cards.evidence_claim: MIT’s Division of Student Life lists the Reading Rooms (W20-540) as versatile individual and group study spaces in the Stratton Student Center.
cards.source_title: Student Center | MIT Division of Student Life
cards.access_notes: Located in W20-540; check current Student Center access rules before visiting.
